title: Museum Exhibition Curator

stages.name: interpretCollection
stages.algorithm: Read artifact records, scholarship, provenance, and conservation guidance to identify what can be responsibly said and displayed. Separate documented facts from contested interpretations and preserve restrictions on handling, light, duration, or cultural presentation.
stages.gate: Every proposed fact and display use has evidence and applicable permission.

stages.name: formNarratives
stages.algorithm: Generate distinct interpretive arguments that connect artifacts meaningfully rather than merely grouping them by topic. Include alternative perspectives and uncertainties, identify missing evidence, and avoid inventing historical continuity to make a more dramatic story.
stages.gate: Narrative claims remain supported and contested interpretations are represented fairly.

stages.name: designVisitorPaths
stages.algorithm: Organize the exhibition into zones and visitor paths that support the argument and audience needs. Offer multiple levels of engagement, preserve accessibility and conservation constraints, and use exact space and flow services for feasibility checks.
stages.gate: Physical layout and artifact constraints are feasible under supplied venue data.

stages.name: writeInterpretation
stages.algorithm: Write labels, introductions, and supporting text that are engaging without overstating evidence. Distinguish fact, attribution, and interpretation, preserve culturally sensitive context, and keep terminology consistent across the visitor journey.
stages.gate: Every material claim is supported or explicitly framed as interpretation.

stages.name: qualifyExhibition
stages.algorithm: Review the complete exhibition for narrative coherence, factual support, rights, conservation, accessibility, and operational feasibility. Compare alternative arrangements, resolve conflicts with qualified owners, and freeze the approved content and installation plan together.
stages.gate: All required specialist approvals and exact physical constraints pass before installation.

operational_details: An artifact loan is withdrawn: revise the argument rather than silently substituting a weaker example.
A label exceeds the available space: shorten without removing a crucial qualification.
A community restriction limits display: enforce it across images, labels, and online previews.
A conservation condition changes: re-evaluate duration and placement.
A visitor skips a zone: ensure later labels do not require inaccessible prior context.

scenario.representative_episode: A small exhibition must connect artifacts with contested provenance, limited display time, and several plausible interpretive narratives.
scenario.independent_truth: Fictional artifact facts, provenance uncertainty, exact venue constraints, rights conditions, and blinded curatorial review.
